questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'New Beginnings: Cities and States' refers to.
questions.a: After the early second millennium BCE, new beginnings reshaped the subcontinent: iron tools cleared forests, villages multiplied, and people gathered into cities and states called janapadas and mahajanapadas.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'New Beginnings: Cities and States'.
questions.a: Better tools and growing surplus let villages grow into cities, and cities into states.

questions.q: Under which section is 'New Beginnings: Cities and States' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Kautilya's Ideal Kingdom' refers to.
questions.a: Kautilya's Arthashastra describes a well-protected kingdom: a fortified capital, cultivable land, mines and forests, water not dependent on rain alone, good roads and a productive economy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Kautilya's Ideal Kingdom'.
questions.a: A strong state plans for hard times: stores, forts and roads keep the people safe in calamities.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Kautilya's Ideal Kingdom' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: The Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha' refers to.
questions.a: Scores of mahajanapadas, each with a capital and an assembly, dotted the subcontinent; Magadha, with its fertile plains, iron and elephants, rose above them all and prepared the ground for empires.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha'.
questions.a: Location plus resources equals power: Magadha's rivers, iron and elephants made it first among states.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Life in the Cities and Villages

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Life in the Cities and Villages' refers to.
questions.a: New cities hummed with artisans, traders and officials, ringed by villages of farmers and herders who paid taxes; coins, weights and writing kept this growing economy moving.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Life in the Cities and Villages'.
questions.a: City and village fed each other: grain flowed in, goods, taxes and orders flowed out.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Life in the Cities and Villages' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Cities and villages (source: gees104.txt, Cities and villages)
